display.title: Episode 452: Reb Yosef Mokir Shabbos
display.summary_short: A listener's letter about turning her house into a mitzvah, Shema with two sisters, and the story of Yosef who honored Shabbos and found a diamond inside his Shabbos fish.
display.summary_long: Uncle Yossi dives into his overflowing mailbox and reads a girl's letter about how her family nailed their tzedakah pushka to the wall, turning their home into a mitzvah, as he suggested on last week's show; she wins a gift certificate, and others are invited to write in. After the Hakochainik march, two sisters from Beis Rivkah recite the Shema and everyone gives tzedakah. Story time opens with Vayechulu and the meaning of Shabbos. Reb Yosef Mokir Shabbos buys the biggest fish in the market every week and shares gefilte fish with the town's poor. A selfish rich man is told by a stargazer that his wealth will pass to Yosef, so he turns it all into one diamond sewn into his hat, which the wind blows into the sea. That Friday a fisherman sells Yosef a giant fish for thirteen gold coins, and inside it is the diamond. As the Sages say, whoever spends for Shabbos is repaid by Shabbos. The show ends with candle-lighting time after the clocks were turned back.
display.lesson: Whatever we spend to honor Shabbos, Hashem repays in full, and riches are meant to be shared with others.

date.note: Candle time 4:25 after the clocks were turned back fits Friday 9 November 1990 in New York; follows episode 450 (Lech Lecha, 23 Oct) and 451. The weekly estimate (23 Oct) was two weeks early.
